reuse.why: The uniqueness, closed-account and takeover rules all go in the shared linkBankSyncAccount, linkFintegraAccount is a thin wrapper over it, and the unlink field reset is pulled out of unlinkAccount into clearBankLink and reused. The Fintegra download, though, does not share any helper with the identical Akahu one.

duplication.why: downloadFintegraTransactions is a verbatim copy of downloadAkahuTransactions with only the server key and log label changed. Smaller repeats: clearBankLink is called in both branches, and the upgrading account is read twice (closed check, then accRow).

placement.why: Link rules live in the common link path in accounts/app.ts, the download sits with the other providers in sync.ts, the server path is in server-config, and types are in models.

scope.why: Focused on the four requests. The client-side provider-map entries are needed for the exhaustive Record/satisfies types, but the release note covers only one of the steps.

maintainability.why: Each rule is defined once in the shared linker with one explicit flag. The provider download copies keep growing one copy per provider.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All link requests go through linkBankSyncAccount, and unlinkAccount now uses clearBankLink.

disguised_duplication.where: The one duplicated block (Fintegra download copied from Akahu) is a plain copy, not disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: linkBankSyncAccount gains only the replaceExistingLink flag. The new checks apply to every provider with no per-provider branches, and no caller goes around the linker.
